2610.08604.title: InterCorrect: Intersection-Aware Correction of Demographic Model Merging for Fair ASR
2610.08604.paper_summary: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems often show uneven performance across demographic groups, and errors can be especially difficult to address for speakers belonging to multiple demographic groups. This work studies demographic-aware model merging for fair Speech-LLM-based ASR. Starting from a SLAM-ASR-based model, we fine-tune only the connector on demographic-specific subsets and merge the resulting subgroup-adapted connectors into a global model. We then identify critical cross-axis demographic pairs using subgroup WER and task-vector conflict, and apply intersection-specific correction vectors to the global merged model. Experiments on Fair-Speech show that global demographic merging improves overall WER over the base model, while intersection correction provides additional gains for several merging strategies. In particular, TIES with WER-based correction achieves the best overall WER, reducing it from 7.38\% to 5.13\%. Subgroup and disparity analyses further show that the proposed approach improves performance across demographic axes, while highlighting that lower average WER does not always imply reduced subgroup disparity.
2610.08604.paper_summary_zh: 自動語音識別（ASR）系統在不同的人口群體中往往表現不均，對於屬於多個人口群體的講者來說，錯誤尤其難以處理。本研究探討了基於人口特徵的模型合併，以實現公平的基於Speech-LLM的ASR。從基於SLAM-ASR的模型開始，我們僅在特定人口子集上微調連接器，並將結果中的子群適應連接器合併到一個全局模型中。然後，我們使用子群WER和任務向量衝突識別關鍵的交叉人口對，並將交集特定的修正向量應用於全局合併模型。對Fair-Speech的實驗顯示，全局人口合併改善了基模型的整體WER，而交集修正則為幾種合併策略提供了額外的增益。特別是，基於WER的修正的TIES達到了最佳的整體WER，將其從7.38\%降低到5.13\%。子群和差異分析進一步顯示，所提出的方法在各人口軸上改善了性能，同時強調較低的平均WER並不總是意味著減少子群差異。
